vanilla_raycast_fluid_none.conversion: A mixin method added to Level overrides BlockGetter's default clip (Mixin 0.8.5 has no injectors in interfaces): for a ClipContext of exactly that class with Fluid.NONE on a level whose class keeps Level.getFluidState, vanilla's own traversal (BlockGetter.traverseBlocks) runs with a step that makes every call of the original step in the same order except the fluid-state read (the fluid shape is asked for the empty fluid state, which NONE never looks at); every other clip calls BlockGetter's default method The added method is an @Intrinsic soft implementation of BlockGetter.m_45547_ in a mixin of priority 1,000,000,000 (applied after every other mixin on Level): if any other mod has given Level its own m_45547_, Mixin keeps theirs and skips ours (generic stand-down, proven offline in evidence/vanilla_raycast/yield-proof.json); the Valkyrien Skies yield below stays.
vanilla_raycast_fluid_none.license: Minecraft (Mojang): no-copy; the mixin and helper carry only our own logic (helper bons.furious.patch.vanilla_raycast.ClipFast)

yields.name: Valkyrien Skies
yields.why: Valkyrien Skies gives Level its own clip too (feature.clip_replace.MixinLevel: shipyard check, then its clipIncludeShips raycast through ships). Both mixins add Level.m_45547_; only one method can exist, and Mixin skips the second with an overwrite-conflict warning, which would drop VS's ship raycasts. Our switch therefore stands down whenever VS's mixin is active (a yield never cancels VS's mixin: that only happens while our switch applies, i.e. without it).
